items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Oh, well they had a fella used to play with me, but he didn't play with no band. His name was Henry Roy.

ctx.x: I'm asking who were some good guitar players before his time.

He said who were some good guitar players before your time? Well, Henry Martin, he was one of the first cups, was the best. Henry Roy, Stonewall, Philip Nicholson, and uh, what's his name? I can't think of his name. I had him landed my tongue. I forgot his name already. Oh yeah, no runs of stow. Yeah, he wasn't my tongue. No. Turn the toe. Yeah, he used to fire him and get me all the time.
Did any of those fellas play with their fingers, finger style, finger picking?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: Me and Henry Roy. Well, that's where Lewis learned all these good stuff from Bunk Johnson, see, after he come out of home.

ctx.x: I asked him which came first.

We had some band, too. Most of our jobs called for white people. We said. We was up three years before we could play for one color people. And the first time we played for color people when Joe Oliver left from the air. You know, the thing I got in there when I was standing right by Joe Oliver with a fellow drumming him, Buddy Sali. Hit him in the eye with a wheel by the hammer. And you know, I thought Joe would be one eye, you know. And he used to have a man, Carol, all them boys. He must have been around about…
I asked you who this Bourne was. That's not Harrison Bourne.
